{{ElectionsHI}}
The '''2026 Hawaii gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Hawaii]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Josh Green (politician)|Josh Green]] is seeking a second term.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|date=May 14, 2026|title=2026 Candidate Report|url=https://olvr.hawaii.gov/Controls/CandidateFiling.aspx?elid=94|access-date=June 1, 2026|website=[[Hawaii Secretary of State]]}}</ref> He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] businessman Gary Cordery.

[[Primary elections]] took place on August 8, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|author=The Sunshine Blog|date=May 9, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260523194629/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-date=May 23, 2026|url-status=live|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]|access-date=August 5, 2025}}</ref> Green secured the Democratic nomination with 88.5% of the vote against three other candidates. Cordery defeated Ken Fujiyama in the Republican primary with 75.9% of the vote. 

Republicans have not won a gubernatorial election in Hawaii since [[2006 Hawaii gubernatorial election|2006]].
